questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

The fraudulent agent managed to __________ several investors __________ their hard-earned savings.
questions.q_hi:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

The fraudulent agent managed to __________ several investors __________ their hard-earned savings.
questions.solution_en:
Explanation: The correct answer is option (3).

English Explanation: “Do out of” means to deprive someone of something, often unfairly or dishonestly. In the sentence, the fraudulent agent deprived several investors of their hard-earned savings. Therefore, “do out of” correctly conveys the idea of cheating or causing someone to lose something they rightfully owned.

It is important to note the structure: do + someone + out of + something. Here, the first blank takes “do” and the second blank takes “out of,” forming the complete phrasal structure:
“The fraudulent agent managed to do several investors out of their hard-earned savings.”

1. Do away with (समाप्त कर देना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी चीज़ को पूरी तरह समाप्त करना।
Example: The company decided to do away with outdated policies. (कंपनी ने पुरानी नीतियों को समाप्त करने का निर्णय लिया।)

2. Do over (दोबारा करना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी कार्य को फिर से करना।
Example: The teacher asked him to do the assignment over. (शिक्षक ने उसे कार्य दोबारा करने को कहा।)

3. Do out of (वंचित कर देना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी को उसकी वस्तु या अधिकार से वंचित करना।
Example 1: His carelessness did him out of a good opportunity in the interview. (उसकी लापरवाही ने उसे एक अच्छे अवसर से वंचित कर दिया।)
Example 2: She was done out of her inheritance by dishonest relatives. (उसे बेईमान रिश्तेदारों ने उसकी विरासत से वंचित कर दिया।)

4. Do up (सजाना / मरम्मत करना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी चीज़ को सजाना, सुधारना या बंद करना।
Example: They plan to do up the old house before selling it. (वे पुराने घर को बेचने से पहले उसकी मरम्मत करेंगे।)

questions.q_en:
Mental health has increasingly entered public discourse, yet its inclusion often remains superficial rather than transformative. Awareness campaigns proliferate, terminology becomes more familiar, and institutions adopt symbolic gestures of concern. However, beneath this apparent progress lies a persistent reluctance to confront the structural and cultural conditions that generate psychological distress. Mental health is frequently treated as an individual malfunction, detached from social environments that normalize chronic stress, insecurity, and emotional suppression. This individualized framing carries subtle consequences. When distress is reduced to personal resilience or chemical imbalance, responsibility quietly shifts away from workplaces, educational systems, and economic arrangements that perpetuate exhaustion and precarity. Coping mechanisms are emphasized over prevention, and adaptation is rewarded more than dissent. In such a framework, the mentally healthy individual is not one who is free from distress, but one who can continue functioning despite it. Institutional responses often mirror this logic. Support systems exist, but access is conditional, fragmented, and reactive. Interventions are triggered once productivity declines or visible crisis emerges, rather than when early signs of strain appear. Moreover, the language of wellness is frequently co-opted to enhance performance rather than well-being, blurring the line between care and control. As a result, mental health initiatives risk becoming tools for sustaining existing norms rather than questioning them. The deeper challenge, therefore, lies in redefining mental health beyond the absence of disorder. It demands recognition of emotional suffering as a rational response to irrational conditions. Without this shift, societies may continue to expand mental health services while simultaneously reproducing the very pressures that make such services indispensable.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

It was hard for the students to __________ all the complex instructions given before the examination.
questions.q_hi:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

It was hard for the students to __________ all the complex instructions given before the examination.
questions.solution_en:
Explanation: The correct answer is option (2).

English Explanation: “Take in” has two important meanings: (1) to absorb or understand information, and (2) to deceive someone. In the sentence, the context clearly refers to students trying to understand complex instructions before the examination. Therefore, “take in” correctly conveys the meaning of mentally absorbing and comprehending information. “Take over” means to assume control of something. “Take up” means to start a new activity or occupy time/space. “Take off” means to remove something or to suddenly become successful. Since the context refers to understanding instructions, “take in” is the most appropriate fit.

1. Take over (नियंत्रण संभाल लेना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी पद, कार्य या संस्था का नियंत्रण अपने हाथ में लेना।
Example: She took over the company after her father retired. (पिता के सेवानिवृत्त होने के बाद उसने कंपनी का नियंत्रण संभाल लिया।)

2. Take in (समझना / आत्मसात करना; धोखा देना)
Meaning in Hindi: जानकारी को समझना या किसी को धोखा देना।
Example 1: It was difficult to take in so many new rules at once. (एक साथ इतने नए नियमों को समझना कठिन था।)
Example 2: He was completely taken in by the fake advertisement. (वह नकली विज्ञापन से पूरी तरह धोखा खा गया।)

3. Take up (शुरू करना / समय लेना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी गतिविधि को शुरू करना या समय/स्थान घेरना।
Example: She took up painting during the holidays. (उसने छुट्टियों में पेंटिंग शुरू की।)

4. Take off (उतारना / अचानक सफल होना)
Meaning in Hindi: कपड़े उतारना या अचानक सफलता प्राप्त करना।
Example: The new product took off in the market. (नया उत्पाद बाजार में अचानक सफल हो गया।)

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The environmental activists argued that the industrial units located near the river
did not upgrade their waste treatment plants to meet the new safety standards
since the National Green Tribunal issued the revised guidelines.
No Error
options_hi: The environmental activists argued that the industrial units located near the river
did not upgrade their waste treatment plants to meet the new safety standards
since the National Green Tribunal issued the revised guidelines.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B).

Replace “did not upgrade” with “have not upgraded”

📌 Rule / Concept: Present Perfect with 'Since' -

If an action of past is used with ‘since’ as a point of time, write that action in past indefinite and main clause in present perfect or present perfect continuous.

💢 Application to the Given Question - The sentence mentions a starting point in the past (the moment the Tribunal issued guidelines — Simple Past). Therefore, the failure to upgrade is a state that has persisted from that moment until the present day. To reflect this duration, the main clause must use the Present Perfect. Thus, "did not upgrade" (Simple Past) must be changed to "have not upgraded" (Present Perfect).

Corrected Sentence - The environmental activists argued that the industrial units located near the river have not upgraded their waste treatment plants to meet the new safety standards since the National Green Tribunal issued the revised guidelines.

More Examples for Clarity -

Example 1 ✅: I have not seen him since he left for London.

Example 2 ✅: Many changes have taken place since she became the CEO.

Example 3 ✅: They have not called us even once since we moved to Delhi.

In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

The Chief Justice remarked that after reviewing the petition, they would decide how the law had been misinterpreted.
questions.q_hi:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

The Chief Justice remarked that after reviewing the petition, they would decide how the law had been misinterpreted.
options_en: The Chief Justice remarked, "After reviewing the petition, they will decide how the law was misinterpreted."
The Chief Justice remarked, "After reviewing the petition, we will decide how the law has been misinterpreted."
The Chief Justice remarked, "After reviewing the petition, we would decide how the law had been misinterpreted."
The Chief Justice remarks, "After reviewing the petition, we will decide how the law is misinterpreted."
options_hi: The Chief Justice remarked, "After reviewing the petition, they will decide how the law was misinterpreted."
The Chief Justice remarked, "After reviewing the petition, we will decide how the law has been misinterpreted."
The Chief Justice remarked, "After reviewing the petition, we would decide how the law had been misinterpreted."
The Chief Justice remarks, "After reviewing the petition, we will decide how the law is misinterpreted."
questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is Option B: The Chief Justice remarked, "After reviewing the petition, we will decide how the law has been misinterpreted."

Tense Back-shift (Reversed):

  • Would -> Will: In Indirect Speech, "would" is used to show a future action from a past perspective. In Direct Speech, this reverts to the simple future "will."

  • Had been -> Has been: The Past Perfect ("had been misinterpreted") in Indirect Speech usually stems from the Present Perfect ("has been misinterpreted") or Simple Past in Direct Speech. Given the context of an ongoing legal review, "has been" is the most accurate fit.

Pronoun Change:

  • They -> We: The pronoun "they" in the Indirect statement refers to the group the Chief Justice is part of (the bench/court). In Direct Speech, the speaker refers to themselves as "we."

questions.q_en:
Identify the grammatical function of the highlighted non-finite phrase.

The students gathered in the auditorium to attend the orientation program conducted by the university administration.
questions.q_hi:
Identify the grammatical function of the highlighted non-finite phrase.

The students gathered in the auditorium to attend the orientation program conducted by the university administration.
questions.solution_en:
Answer: C) Functioning as an adverb

Explanation: An infinitive phrase can function as a noun, adjective, or adverb.

The highlighted phrase:

“to attend the orientation program conducted by the university administration” modifies the verb “gathered” and tells the purpose of gathering.

gathered why? → to attend the orientation program

Therefore, the phrase functions as an adverb.

Why other options are incorrect:

A) A noun functions as subject/object/complement.

B) An adjective modifies a noun/pronoun, but this phrase modifies the verb “gathered.”

D) The subject of the sentence is “The students.”

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: Nature’s fury was unleashed upon the coastal village,
as the waves reached for the sky and the wind shrieked
like a wounded beast through the narrow, deserted streets.
No Error
options_hi: Nature’s fury was unleashed upon the coastal village,
as the waves reached for the sky and the wind shrieked
like a wounded beast through the narrow, deserted streets.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (D) - No Error.

Rule/Concept: Personification in Possessives -

-In standard English grammar, the possessive case ('s) is typically reserved for living things (e.g., the boy's book). However, an exception is made for Personified Objects.

-When we attribute human qualities, emotions, or actions to inanimate objects or abstract nouns, they are treated as living entities and can take the apostrophe 's.

Common categories that allow this include:

-Nature/Natural phenomena: Nature's fury, the sun's rays.

-Time/Distance/Weight: A day's march, a stone's throw.

-Dignified/Personified entities: The law's arm, the nation's soul, the ocean's roar.

Application to the Given Question - Nature’s fury was unleashed... the wind shrieked like a wounded beast...

In this sentence, "Nature" is being treated as a conscious entity capable of feeling and expressing "fury." Furthermore, the wind is given the human-like action of "shrieking." Because Nature is being personified here as a powerful, vengeful force, using the possessive Nature's is grammatically correct and stylistically appropriate for high-level English.

Things to Remember / Exam Tips

-The "Living" Test: If the object is inanimate and not being personified (like a chair, table, or car), use the "of" phrase (the legs of the chair).

-The "Dignity" Test: Abstract nouns that carry a sense of power or personification (Duty, Justice, Mercy, Nature, Country) are safe to use with an apostrophe.

-Trap Alert: Examiners often mix "The Sun's rays" (Correct) with "The Table's wood" (Incorrect) to confuse students on the limits of this rule.

-When we attribute human qualities, emotions, or actions to inanimate objects or abstract nouns, they are treated as living entities and can take the apostrophe 's.

Common categories that allow this include:

-Nature/Natural phenomena: Nature's fury, the sun's rays.

-Time/Distance/Weight: A day's march, a stone's throw.

-Dignified/Personified entities: The law's arm, the nation's soul, the ocean's roar.

Application to the Given Question - Nature’s fury was unleashed... the wind shrieked like a wounded beast...

In this sentence, "Nature" is being treated as a conscious entity capable of feeling and expressing "fury." Furthermore, the wind is given the human-like action of "shrieking." Because Nature is being personified here as a powerful, vengeful force, using the possessive Nature's is grammatically correct and stylistically appropriate for high-level English.

Things to Remember / Exam Tips

-The "Living" Test: If the object is inanimate and not being personified (like a chair, table, or car), use the "of" phrase (the legs of the chair).

-The "Dignity" Test: Abstract nouns that carry a sense of power or personification (Duty, Justice, Mercy, Nature, Country) are safe to use with an apostrophe.

-Trap Alert: Examiners often mix "The Sun's rays" (Correct) with "The Table's wood" (Incorrect) to confuse students on the limits of this rule.

The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

Although he lacks the formal credentials of a scientist, his innovative approach to solving environmental issues proves that he is _________ Edison in his own right.
questions.q_hi:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

Although he lacks the formal credentials of a scientist, his innovative approach to solving environmental issues proves that he is _________ Edison in his own right.
questions.solution_en:
Rule / Concept: Proper Nouns used as Common Nouns-

When a proper noun (the name of a specific person or place) is used as a common noun to represent a specific quality or to compare a person to a well-known figure, an indefinite article (A/An) or the definite article (The) is used before it.

The choice between A and An depends entirely on the sound of the first letter of that proper noun.

Application to the Given Question- "...his innovative approach to solving environmental issues proves that he is an Edison in his own right."

Things to Remember / Exam Tips-

1. The Comparison Logic: Using "A/An" suggests "a person possessing the qualities of." Using "The" suggests "the specific equivalent of."

2. Sound Over Spelling: Never forget that this Rule is still subject to the vowel/consonant sound rule. For example, "a University" vs "an Honest man."

More Examples for Clarity-

1. He is a Newton of our class. (General comparison of intelligence)

2. He is the Newton of this century. (Specific comparison)

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: Despite his immense interest in classical music,
the young prodigy usually has not practiced
his violin lessons for more than an hour daily.
options_hi: Despite his immense interest in classical music,
the young prodigy usually has not practiced
his violin lessons for more than an hour daily.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B) Replace “has not” with “does not”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Simple Present for Habitual Actions

When a sentence describes a habit, routine, or frequency, we must use the Simple Present Tense . Adverbs of frequency such as usually, often, seldom, daily, always, and never act as "tense markers" that point toward the Simple Present.

Using the Present Perfect is incorrect here because the Present Perfect is used for actions that happened at an unspecified time in the past or have just been completed. It does not denote a general habit.

💢 Application to the Given Question

"...the young prodigy usually has not practiced his violin lessons for more than an hour daily."

The sentence contains two major indicators of a habit:

  1. The word "usually" (denoting frequency).

  2. The word "daily" (denoting a routine).

Because the sentence is describing the prodigy's regular routine (or lack thereof), we must use the negative form of the Simple Present. Since "the young prodigy" is a singular subject, we use "does not" followed by the base form of the verb (practice).

Corrected Sentence

Despite his immense interest in classical music, the young prodigy usually does not practice his violin lessons for more than an hour daily.
